title: Baseline the checks on the base commit; mark failures pre-existing
summary: Before the producer starts, Athena runs the capability's checks on the base commit and records which fail. At verification, a check failing at the base is marked pre-existing and no longer rejects the job; the verifier now runs and judges every criterion even when a check fails. A check that fails only on the candidate still fails the job. The audience is Athena's operator and the verifier reading job records.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require new tests and a clean cargo test, clippy and fmt.
Behavior criteria name the verdicts and records that must result.
The verdict logic is changed, not a single check special-cased.
One change on the check and verdict path.
Records and rejection reasons state pre-existing versus new failures.
Criteria check the verdict outcome, not that the wiring exists.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Today run.rs only starts the verifier when every check passed (`if all_passed`), so one failing check leaves all criteria unassessed; that is the behavior to change.
'Pre-existing' means the same-named check failed on the base commit; a check is pre-existing only if it also fails on the candidate.
A new check failure still fails the job, but the verifier runs anyway so criteria are judged individually.
The base run reuses the same check specs, environment, timeout and kill switch as candidate checks, in a snapshot of the base.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test shows a job whose base commit fails a check (for example fmt) still reaches the verifier, the record marks that check pre-existing, and the final verdict can be pass. Run `cargo test`.
A new test shows a check that passes at the base and fails on the candidate is not marked pre-existing and still makes the final verdict fail. Run `cargo test`.
A new test shows that when a non-pre-existing check fails, the verifier still runs and every acceptance criterion gets its own met or unmet result, instead of all being unassessed. Run `cargo test`.
A test shows the base-commit check run happens before the producer starts and its failing check names are written to the job record. Run `cargo test`.
A check that fails on the candidate with a different failure than at the base is not hidden. If the test check runs fewer or zero tests, it is not treated as pre-existing. `cargo test` covers this.
The verification record shows each check's pre-existing status, and a stranger reading the verifier brief or the rejection reasons can see which failures were pre-existing and which were new.
The CheckRun record change stays readable for existing stored records, with a default for the new field, and CHANGELOG.md describes the new behavior.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass on the candidate. Any that fail at the base are reported as pre-existing.

out_of_scope: Changing athena.toml check definitions or CI workflows
Changing how the verifier is allowed to run commands
departures: Higher cost and time than the reference: the change spans run.rs (a large file), verdict logic, a stored record schema and several new tests.
